title: The Hollow of the Weeping Wood
premise: Casper Lockridge has spent a decade mapping the Thornfell mountains for the Crown while quietly selling safe routes to smugglers, keeping herself useful to everyone and loyal to no one. When a mute child appears at her door speaking the dead tongue of the Weald—the forest the kingdoms burned to win their borders—Casper realizes the girl is a vessel of the old wood's memory, and that the Crown's cartographers' guild is hunting her to finish what the war started. Torn between the guildmaster who once saved her life and the smugglers who have become her only true family, Casper must choose whether to deliver the child or carry her into the Hollow, the heart of the weeping wood where the forest's last spirit sleeps. In the end, Casper surrenders her maps—her life's work and her invisibility—to the flames of the Hollow, waking the Weald and erasing every road she ever drew, buying the child a future at the cost of everything Casper built to survive.
about_author: Yara Thornbury is the pen name of a former trail surveyor who spent six years walking the border ranges that inspired the Thornfell mountains. She writes fantasy rooted in real landscapes, where maps are promises and forests remember.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Spoke Before Kingdoms
chapters.summary: POV Casper. A storm-battered child arrives at Casper's remote survey cabin speaking a language no living scholar knows—and the words make the candle flames bend toward her. Casper, who survived by never being noticed, feels the first pull of a choice she can't map. Emotional beat: wary wonder cracking open a guarded heart.

chapters.title: Ink and Obligation
chapters.summary: POV Casper. The Crown's cartographers' guild summons Casper to Thornfell Keep, where guildmaster Aldous Vane—her old mentor and savior—shows her reports of 'forest signs' in the mountains and asks her to find their source. She realizes the hunt is already aimed at the child. Emotional beat: dread beneath practiced calm; loyalty to Vane curdling into conflict.

chapters.title: What the Smugglers Know
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Seeking allies, Casper brings the child to Bren the ferryman and his smuggler crew, who recognize fragments of the language from songs their grandmothers were forbidden to sing. The child speaks her first translated word: 'Hollow.' Emotional beat: found-family warmth shadowed by the knowledge that harboring the girl is treason.

chapters.title: The Road That Isn't There
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Guild riders sweep the passes, and Casper uses a smuggler's road she never inked onto any official map to slip the child through. But someone has copied her private charts—only three people could have. Emotional beat: paranoia and betrayal; the dawning cost of having trusted anyone at all.

chapters.title: Songs Under the Root
chapters.summary: POV Bren. Sheltering in an abandoned mine shrine, Bren tells Casper how the Weald was burned and its people scattered, and why his family kept the old tongue alive in secret. The child dreams aloud in her sleep, and the mine walls bloom with moss. Emotional beat: grief transformed into resolve; love against duty taking root.

chapters.title: Vane's Bargain
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Vane corners Casper alone: he knows she has the child. He offers pardon and protection if she delivers the girl to the guild—for the Crown believes the Weald's spirit, once captured, will end famine and war forever. He genuinely believes it. Emotional beat: the terrible reasonableness of duty; Casper almost says yes.

chapters.title: The Copyist
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Casper discovers the traitor: young apprentice Ilsa, who copied the charts not for gold but because Vane promised to legitimize her bastard name. Confronting her, Casper sees her own younger self—and lets her go with a warning instead of a knife. Emotional beat: mercy as rebellion; loyalty vs. truth made flesh.

chapters.title: Flight Through the Weeping Wood
chapters.summary: POV Casper. With guild riders and Vane himself behind them, Casper and the smugglers drive a cart into the dead forest at night. Trees that died a century ago shudder awake as the child passes, weeping sap like tears. The rearguard fight costs Bren a hand. Emotional beat: terror and awe entwined; no turning back now.

chapters.title: The Hollow
chapters.summary: POV Casper. At the forest's heart, the child reveals the truth: she is not the spirit's vessel but its seed, and it can only wake if fed something truly given up. Vane arrives, blade drawn, still pleading the Crown's case. Casper casts her life's work—every map, every secret road—into the Hollow's spring. Emotional beat: climax; sacrifice as the only honest currency.

chapters.title: Where No Road Goes
chapters.summary: POV Casper, months later. The Weald is green again, its people returning, and the Crown's armies cannot enter a forest that rearranges itself around them. Casper, mapless and anonymous at last by choice rather than fear, teaches the child—now speaking plainly—to draw her own first map. Emotional beat: quiet resolution; survival's price paid, and worth it.
